title: Bunk and Bechet at Ryan's on teaching Louis
summary: At Ryan's and Bickford's, Bunk and Bechet trade tunes and Bechet confirms Bunk taught Louis; Bunk teases Sidney about an old girl.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: He'd do things like that repeatedly, yeah. If I remember the other night you mentioned something, some detail escapes me now about Bechet and speaking about when he helped Louis and all that. That's right.

What was that? Well, there was a time when Bechet was playing at Ryan's and Harold Draub and a friend of mine from Baltimore and myself went into Ryan's to see Bechet and Bunk turned up and he had been drinking very heavily. And he was closer in the disorder that they often got in at such times. And he was sitting at our table and then he'd get up to the bandstand and be singing along with the tune. And he was having some kind of contest with Sidney about what... Trying to name tunes that Sidney couldn't remember. But Sidney seemed to be able to remember everything that Bunk was trying to catch him on, you know. It was very, very good. And they played a bunch of tunes that I never heard before or since. I mean, just really obscure old tunes. And finally, after the evening was over, the five of us went to the cafeteria at Bickford's, I think it was. And it was Sidney and Bunk and Harold and my friend and myself. And Bunk was saying to Sidney, talking about teaching Louis and how Louis was denying that he had taken lessons. And Bunk says, don't you remember Sidney when I was giving lessons to Louis and you would be there? And Sidney says, yeah, you know. And Sidney agreed with him 100% that he had taught Louis.
Actually helped him with his horn.
And that he had taught Sidney too. I don't know how much he taught him, but he said that Sidney agreed that he had been a pupil, a music pupil of Bunk.
Did Bunk and Ply actually help Louis with his horn in addition to just playing for him or letting him follow him?

Well, he said taught him, I mean, and that's what Sidney agreed to, you know. So I got the idea it was lessons, I mean, you know, that they had come to Bunk, you know, to take a music lesson. That's the idea I got. I mean, you might ask Harold about it because he remembers these things more clearly, more verbatim than I do, but I'm sure he would remember this particular episode. He was there then. Yeah. But it was nice to see that Bunk and Sidney had made up too, you know.
Yeah, that was considerably later than their Boston fiasco.

Yeah. He was calling him Sidley, Sidley, and he was talking to him like you talk to a little kid, you know. And Sidney, whose dignity was not accustomed to such a position, was kind of embarrassed. But after a while he just realized he had to take it, so he stood up pretty well. And Bunk accused Sidney of going out with Bunk's girl here in New Orleans back maybe 50 years before, you know. And Bunk says, I know about you. I know that you used to date this girl, you know. And Sidney says, well tell me Bunk. He says, how come you never mentioned it to me before? I said that happened 50 years ago or whenever it was. We thought it was kind of funny, you know. He suddenly comes up with this accusation.
It really had been Bunk's girl then I guess. Yeah, yeah. Sidney didn't deny it either. No, he agreed.

He had been guilty. But he says, how come you never mentioned it to me before? Apparently Bunk never mentioned it to me the whole Boston thing. Yeah. It's a matter he didn't throw it up there when they were arguing all the time.
